text: Timotheo caro filio gratiam, misericordiam, pacem a Deo Patre, et Christo Jesu Domino nostro.
note: *Patre* capital, God the Father (decision 20; ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πατρός, NRSV and BSB *God the Father*), as Gal 1:3 and your 1 Cor 1:3 *ā Deō Patre*; the greeting runs on from the address without a stop (*fīliō grātiam*), as 1573 prints it (*Timotheo charo filio gratiam, / misericordiam, pacem, à Deo pa-/tre*, canvas 912), so *grātiam* stays lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: nunc repraesentatum est adventu Servatoris nostri Jesu Christi, qui et mortem abolevit, et vitam ac immortalitatem collustravit per evangelium,
note: *Servātōris* capital, Christ the Saviour (decision 20; τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, NRSV *our Savior Christ Jesus*), as your settled Eph 5:23 *Servātor*, Phil 3:20, Luke 2:11, John 4:42, Acts 5:31 and 13:23 *Servātōrem* (6 : 0 for Christ); *nunc* lower case, the sentence of 1:9 running on (written here, as a capital changed in a layout line stops the pipeline's own lowering) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Aversati sunt me (hoc tu nosti) omnes Asiani, quorum est Phygelus et Hermogenes.
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 1:14 ends the charge to guard the deposit (1:13–14) with a full stop and *Āversātī sunt mē* turns to news of Paul's companions, the deserters of Asia and the loyal Onesiphorus (1:15–18), a new step, as the NRSV's paragraph (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Recordare Jesum Christum ex mortuis excitatum, Davidis semine prognatum, ut fert evangelium meum,
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 2:7 closes the three likenesses of soldier, athlete and farmer (2:3–7) with a full stop and *Recordāre Jēsum Chrīstum* (Μνημόνευε) turns to the gospel Paul suffers for (2:8–13), a new step, as the NRSV's paragraph (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Certa res est: \\q1 si simul mortui sumus, \\q2 simul etiam vivemus.
note: paragraph and poetry (the BSB's b m, then *\\b \\q1* after *This is a trustworthy saying:*): *Certa rēs est* (Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος) introduces the saying of 2:11b–13, which the BSB sets as verse in four couplets and a closing line; set the same way, two lines to each *sī* clause as the Latin's order allows; a saying, not Scripture, so no \\qt and no quotation marks, as Phil 2:6–11 and your settled Rom 11:33–36; *sī* lower case after the colon, as the draft and 1573 (*Certa res eſt : ſi ſimul*, canvas 913) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Si una toleramus, \\q2 etiam una regnabimus. \\q1 Si negamus, \\q2 ille quoque negabit nos:
note: the saying continued as poetry, two couplets after the BSB (*if we endure, / we will also reign with Him; / if we deny Him, / He will also deny us*); capitals as the draft and 1573 (*Si vnà toleramus … Si ne-/gamus*) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Si diffidimus, \\q2 ille fidelis manet, \\q2 se ipsum negare non potest.
note: the saying's last three lines, as the BSB (*if we are faithless, / He remains faithful, / for He cannot deny Himself*); *Sī* keeps the draft's capital after 2:12's colon, as your settled books do after a colon (1573 lower case *ſi diffidimus*); 2:14's paragraph (the draft's) closes the poetry (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Atqui firmum Dei fundamentum stat, hoc habens sigillum: \\qt “Novit Dominus qui sint sui”\\qt*: itaque recedat ab injustitia, quisquis nominat Christi nomen.
note: *Nōvit Dominus quī sint suī* is Num 16:5 (LXX Ἔγνω ὁ θεὸς τοὺς ὄντας αὐτοῦ; the BSB quotes it), the seal's inscription after *hoc habēns sigillum:*: in \\qt with “…”, prose; *Nōvit* capital as the quotation's first word and as 1573 prints it (*figillum : Nouit Dominus qui fint fui*, canvas 913). The second clause, which the BSB also quotes (Isa 26:13 / Sir 17:26 in substance, no verse in these words), is left unmarked: Castellio turns the Greek's καί, into *itaque*, making it Paul's inference from the first; **uncertain**, it can be read as the seal's second inscription (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Juveniles cupiditates fuge: justitiam, fidem, caritatem, pacem una cum iis, qui Dominum sincero animo invocant, persequere.
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 2:21 ends the likeness of the vessels in a great house (2:20–21) with a full stop and *Juvenīlēs cupiditātēs fuge* turns to direct commands to Timothy (2:22–26), a new step, as the NRSV's paragraph (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: pietatis speciem habentes, sed qui ejus vim abnegaverint. Hos tu aversare.
note: *pietātis* lower case: the list of 3:2–4 runs on (3:4 ends *amantēs,*; ἔχοντες agrees with οἱ ἄνθρωποι of 3:2), as 1573 prints it (*pietatis ſpeciem habentes*, canvas 913); the pipeline left the draft's capital (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Tu vero in eis persevera, quae didicisti, et per quae fidens factus es, quum et scias, a quo didiceris,
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 3:13 ends the picture of the impostors with a full stop and *Tū vērō* (Σὺ δέ) turns back to Timothy and the Scriptures he has known from childhood (3:14–17), a new step, as the NRSV's paragraph (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Demas enim me, vitae praesentis amore, dereliquit, et Thessalonicam profectus est: Crescens in Galatiam: Titus in Dalmatiam:
note: a comma after *mē*, as 1573 (*Demas enim me , vitæ præſentis amore , dereli-quit*, canvas 914): without it the draft's lone comma after *amōre* parts the object *mē* from its verb; *vītæ præsentis amōre* stands as the participle's phrase (ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα) between the two (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Alexander faber ferrarius multis me malis adfecit: reddat ei Dominus digna ejus factis praemia.
note: paragraph (the BSB's b m): 4:13 ends Paul's requests for himself (4:9–13) with a full stop and the warning about Alexander (4:14–15) is a new step, as the NRSV's paragraph; the comma after *ferrārius* dropped, as 1573 (*Alexander faber ferrarius multis me malis affe-cit*, canvas 914): it parted the subject from its verb (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Dominus Jesus Christus adsit animo tuo. Adsit vobis gratia: Amen. \\cls Scripta est Romae ad Timotheum secunda, quum se Paulus iterum stitisset Caesari Neroni.
note: the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as 1573 sets it apart under the blessing (*Adſit vobis gratia : Amen .*, then on lines of their own *Scripta est Rome ad Timotheum …, / cùm se Paulus iterum ſtitiſſet / Cæſari Neroni .*, canvas 914) and as your Rom 16:27, 1 Cor 16:24, 2 Cor 13:14 and Gal 6:18; the colon before *Āmēn* kept, as 1573 and the draft; a full stop added at the end, as 1573 (the draft has none) (Claude, 2026-11-11)
